neighbours.label: a hard line break inside a running sentence (wrapped prose, the newline right after a function word)
fire:
This booklet is written for parents who want to know more about
the early years of their child's schooling.

Visitors who wish to explore the gardens should start at
the north gate and follow the gravel path.

The report describes the main causes of the flooding and
the steps the town has taken since then.

Many of the early settlers came from farming villages in
the south and brought their customs with them.

Students are expected to read the first three chapters of
the textbook before the seminar begins.

The museum holds a large collection of tools used by
the miners who worked in the valley.

Our volunteers spend most weekends cleaning the banks of
the river near the old mill.

The committee will review all of the proposals and
announce its decision in the spring.
quiet:
This booklet is written for parents of young children.
It covers the first years of school.

Visitors are welcome in the gardens every day.
The north gate opens at nine.

The report describes the main causes of the flooding.
It also lists the town's plans.

Many of the early settlers were farmers.
They brought their customs with them.

Students should read three chapters this week.
The seminar begins on Monday.

The museum holds a large collection of mining tools.
Most of them are over a century old.

Our volunteers clean the river banks most weekends.
They meet near the old mill.

The committee will review all of the proposals.
Its decision is due in the spring.

notes: Card: '\n' x23 of the top 32, nearly all hard wraps mid-sentence; the + pole also peaks on wrap newlines, so the split between poles is not clear. Probes on wrapped prose were mixed (0.55 on one, ~0.01-0.02 on others). Near misses break only at sentence ends.
